title: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL)
subtitle: B-ALL (Ph+ / Ph-) and T-ALL Lineages with Risk, MRD, and Targeted Immunotherapy
provenanceNote: Clinical algorithms extracted from NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
sourceNote: NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 - Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL-1 to ALL-8, ALL-D)

footnotes.fn_mrd: Preferred MRD method is FDA-approved NGS or multiparametric flow cytometry (<0.01% threshold).
footnotes.fn_blina: Blinatumomab should be incorporated into consolidation for Ph- B-ALL based on ECOG 1910 data.

nodes.name: Diagnosis of ALL
nodes.title: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: Diagnosis & Initial Classification
nodes.description: Demonstration of >=20% bone marrow lymphoblasts on hematopathology review (aspirate smears, core biopsy, clot sections).
bullets: Morphologic assessment of Wright-Giemsa-stained bone marrow aspirate smears and H&E-stained core biopsy/clot sections.
Comprehensive flow cytometric immunophenotyping to establish B-cell vs T-cell lineage and baseline leukemic clone profile.
Conventional G-banded metaphase karyotype (minimum 20 metaphases).
Interphase FISH testing: detect recurrent genomic abnormalities including BCR::ABL1, KMT2A, ETV6::RUNX1, TCF3::PBX1, and iAMP21.
RT-PCR for BCR::ABL1 (determine p190 vs p210 transcript size) and multigene NGS panel for fusions and pathogenic variants.

options.label: Diagnosis confirmed - Proceed to mandatory pre-treatment workup

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: ALL Mandatory Clinical & Laboratory Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Baseline organ function, coagulopathy screening, CNS staging, and infection/cardiac risk assessment prior to induction.
bullets: Complete blood count (CBC) with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel (LFTs, renal function, electrolytes).
Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) panel: PT/INR, PTT, fibrinogen, D-dimer (essential before invasive procedures).
Tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) panel: LDH, uric acid, potassium, calcium, phosphorus; initiate hydration +/- rasburicase or allopurinol.
Infectious disease screening: Hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs), Hepatitis C Ab, HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab; screen for active opportunistic infections.
Lumbar puncture (LP) with CSF cell count, differential, and cytology + initial prophylactic intrathecal (IT) chemotherapy (methotrexate, cytarabine, or triple therapy).
Echocardiogram or cardiac MUGA scan: baseline LVEF assessment mandatory prior to high-dose anthracycline chemotherapy.
Imaging: CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast or whole-body FDG-PET/CT if lymphomatous involvement suspected. Brain MRI if neurologic symptoms.
Testicular examination: bilateral scrotal palpation; obtain scrotal ultrasound if mass or asymmetry noted.
Reproductive counseling: pregnancy test in females of childbearing potential; offer sperm/oocyte cryopreservation before cytotoxic therapy.
Central venous access: place durable tunneled catheter or PICC line; initiate HLA typing for patient and full siblings for early allogeneic HCT planning.

options.label: Workup completed - Classify immunophenotype and lineage

nodes.name: Lineage Classification
nodes.title: Leukemic Lineage & Immunophenotype
nodes.description: Flow cytometry immunophenotyping distinguishes B-lineage from T-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
bullets: B-ALL: Positive for CD19, CD22, CD79a, PAX5; CD10 (common ALL antigen); CD20 variable (positive in ~30-50%).
T-ALL: Positive for cytoplasmic and/or surface CD3, CD7, CD2, CD5; early T-cell precursor (ETP) subtype typically lacks CD1a and CD8.

options.label: B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B-ALL)
T-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (T-ALL)

nodes.name: Philadelphia Chromosome Status
nodes.title: B-ALL: Cytogenetic and Molecular Risk Stratification
nodes.description: Detection of t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) BCR::ABL1 fusion defines Ph-positive vs Ph-negative B-ALL.
bullets: Ph-positive (BCR::ABL1 positive): detected by karyotype t(9;22), interphase FISH, or RT-PCR (p190 or p210 transcript). Mandates TKI incorporation into induction.
Ph-negative (BCR::ABL1 negative): risk stratify by cytogenetics (standard risk: hyperdiploidy 51-65, ETV6::RUNX1, DUX4-r; poor risk: hypodiploidy <44, KMT2A-r, TP53, Ph-like fusions).

options.label: Philadelphia Chromosome Positive (Ph+ B-ALL / BCR::ABL1+)
Philadelphia Chromosome Negative (Ph- B-ALL / BCR::ABL1-)

nodes.name: Ph+ ALL Patient Fitness
nodes.title: Ph+ B-ALL: Age & Comorbidity Stratification
nodes.description: Select induction intensity based on patient age, ECOG performance status, and cardiac/vascular comorbidity profile.
bullets: AYA & Adults <65 years without substantial comorbidities: intensive chemotherapy + potent TKI (dasatinib or ponatinib) OR chemotherapy-free TKI + blinatumomab.
Adults >=65 years or adults with substantial comorbidities: low-intensity backbone (TKI + blinatumomab OR TKI + corticosteroids/vincristine OR mini-hyper-CVD + TKI).

options.label: AYA & Adults <65 years without substantial comorbidities (Fit)
Adults >=65 years or adults with substantial comorbidities (Frail/Unfit)

nodes.name: Ph+ Fit Induction
nodes.title: Ph+ B-ALL (Fit): Frontline Induction Selection
nodes.description: Frontline TKI-based induction regimens for fit Ph+ B-ALL patients.
bullets: Chemo-free BiTE approach (Preferred): Ponatinib (30 mg daily, reduced to 15 mg in CMR) or Dasatinib (140 mg daily) + Blinatumomab (continuous IV infusion) + IT chemotherapy (methotrexate/cytarabine).

Intensive Chemo-TKI: Hyper-CVAD (hyperfractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, dexamethasone alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine) + Ponatinib or Dasatinib + IT chemotherapy.
Rituximab addition: If blasts express CD20 >=20%, add rituximab to chemotherapy cycles to improve event-free survival.
Supportive care: Prophylactic anticoagulation / vascular monitoring if ponatinib used; antimicrobial prophylaxis (levofloxacin, posaconazole/voriconazole, acyclovir, Bactrim).

options.label: Induction administered - Proceed to post-induction response & MRD evaluation

nodes.name: Ph+ Frail Induction
nodes.title: Ph+ B-ALL (Frail / Elderly): Low-Intensity Induction Selection
nodes.description: Low-to-moderate intensity TKI-based frontline regimens designed to minimize treatment-related mortality.
bullets: TKI + Blinatumomab (Preferred low-intensity): Dasatinib or Ponatinib combined with blinatumomab; high CR rate with minimal myelosuppression.
TKI + Corticosteroid: Dasatinib (140 mg daily) or Ponatinib (30 mg daily) + Dexamethasone/Prednisone taper (GIMEMA or EWALL backbone).
TKI + Vincristine/Dexamethasone: Low-dose weekly vincristine with short pulse dexamethasone + TKI.
Moderate intensity: Mini-hyper-CVD (attenuated dose cyclophosphamide, vincristine, dexamethasone without anthracycline) + TKI.

options.label: Induction administered - Proceed to post-induction response & MRD evaluation

nodes.name: Ph+ Post-Induction Response
nodes.title: Ph+ B-ALL: Morphologic & MRD Response Assessment
nodes.description: Bone marrow biopsy at day 28-35 to assess morphologic CR (<5% blasts, count recovery) and quantifiable MRD by NGS or RT-PCR.
bullets: Complete Remission (CR): <5% bone marrow blasts, absence of peripheral blasts, absence of extramedullary disease, ANC >=1000/mcL, platelets >=100,000/mcL.
MRD quantification: high-sensitivity RT-PCR for BCR::ABL1 (target major molecular response MMR / complete molecular response CMR) or NGS-based clonality assay (sensitivity 10^-6).
Persistent positivity at induction end requires ABL1 kinase domain sequencing for resistance mutations (e.g., T315I, Y253H, E255K/V).

options.label: Complete Remission (CR) with MRD Negative (Complete Molecular Remission)
Complete Remission (CR) with Persistent MRD Positive
Primary Refractory Disease / Less than CR (>5% blasts)

nodes.name: Ph+ MRD- Consolidation
nodes.title: Ph+ B-ALL: MRD-Negative Consolidation & Maintenance
nodes.description: Consolidation strategy for patients achieving deep molecular remission.
bullets: Allogeneic HCT decision: Consider allogeneic HCT in eligible candidates with IKZF1plus alterations, high-risk features, or slower molecular kinetics, followed by post-HCT TKI maintenance.

Non-transplant consolidation (TKI maintenance pathway): In patients achieving early complete molecular response (CMR) with potent TKIs (ponatinib/dasatinib) or ineligible for HCT, continued TKI + POMP maintenance (or blinatumomab consolidation cycles) produces durable leukemia-free survival.

Maintenance therapy: TKI daily (ponatinib 15 mg daily or dasatinib 100-140 mg daily) for a minimum of 5 years (or indefinitely), with or without POMP maintenance (mercaptopurine daily, methotrexate weekly, vincristine + prednisone monthly pulses) for 2-3 years.
Intrathecal CNS prophylaxis: Continue IT chemotherapy as scheduled per protocol (minimum 8-12 total doses across induction, consolidation, and early maintenance).
Molecular monitoring: Serial quantitative RT-PCR for BCR::ABL1 every 3 months for at least 3-5 years.

nodes.name: Ph+ MRD+ Intensification
nodes.title: Ph+ B-ALL: Persistent MRD Intensification & Bridge to HCT
nodes.description: Targeted intensification for persistent minimal residual disease.
bullets: ABL1 Kinase Domain Mutation Testing: Immediately sequence the BCR::ABL1 kinase domain to detect emergent gatekeeper (T315I) or P-loop mutations.
TKI switch: If T315I mutation identified, switch to ponatinib (45 mg daily) or asciminib; switch dasatinib to ponatinib if other resistant clones emerge.
Blinatumomab + TKI (Preferred): Initiate blinatumomab (continuous IV infusion x 28-day cycle) in combination with active TKI to eradicate residual clone.
Allogeneic HCT: Strongly recommended for all eligible patients once MRD clearance or lowest possible disease burden is attained.
Alternative intensification: Multiagent chemotherapy consolidation (high-dose methotrexate/cytarabine) + TKI if blinatumomab unavailable.

nodes.name: Ph- B-ALL Age & Fitness
nodes.title: Ph- B-ALL: Age & Protocol Cohort Stratification
nodes.description: Patient age and physiological fitness dictate whether pediatric-inspired, standard adult, or dose-reduced regimens are used.
bullets: AYA (Adolescent & Young Adult, 15-39 years) without substantial comorbidities: pediatric-inspired regimens (high-dose asparaginase, vincristine, corticosteroids, methotrexate) significantly improve event-free survival.
Adults 40-64 years without substantial comorbidities: intensive adult multiagent chemotherapy (ECOG 1910 backbone, Hyper-CVAD) +/- rituximab.
Adults >=65 years or with substantial comorbidities: dose-attenuated chemotherapy (mini-hyper-CVD, POMP, low-dose vincristine/prednisone) or inotuzumab-based therapy.

options.label: AYA (Age 15–39 years) without substantial comorbidities
Adults (Age 40–64 years) without substantial comorbidities
Adults >=65 years or adults with substantial comorbidities

nodes.name: Ph- AYA Induction
nodes.title: Ph- B-ALL: AYA Pediatric-Inspired Frontline Regimens
nodes.description: Pediatric-inspired intensive multiagent chemotherapy protocols.
bullets: CALGB 10403 (Preferred): 5-drug induction consisting of daunorubicin, vincristine, prednisone, pegaspargase (or calaspargase pegol if <=21y), and cyclophosphamide + IT methotrexate.
DFCI ALL Protocol 00-01: Doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone, pegaspargase, high-dose methotrexate, and 6-mercaptopurine.
COG AALL0232 / CCG-1882 inspired regimens.

Asparaginase toxicity management: Monitor antithrombin III, fibrinogen, amylase/lipase, and LFTs. If clinical allergy or neutralizing antibodies occur, substitute Erwinia asparaginase (crisantaspase / ERW-rywn).
CNS prophylaxis: Intrathecal methotrexate or triple IT (methotrexate, cytarabine, hydrocortisone) delivered at scheduled timepoints.

options.label: Induction completed - Proceed to response and MRD assessment

nodes.name: Ph- Adult Induction
nodes.title: Ph- B-ALL: Adult Multiagent Frontline Regimens (Age 40–64)
nodes.description: Multiagent induction backbones with incorporation of immunotherapy.
bullets: ECOG-ACRIN E1910 backbone (Preferred): Multiagent induction (daunorubicin, vincristine, prednisone, pegaspargase, cyclophosphamide) with sequential blinatumomab consolidation.
Hyper-CVAD: Hyperfractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, dexamethasone alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine.
CD20-Directed Monoclonal Antibody: For CD20-positive B-ALL (>=20% blast expression), add rituximab to chemotherapy cycles (GRAALL-2005 / GMALL data).
CNS prophylaxis: Regular IT chemotherapy (methotrexate 12 mg or cytarabine 100 mg or triple IT) with each chemotherapy course.

options.label: Induction completed - Proceed to response and MRD assessment

nodes.name: Ph- Frail Induction
nodes.title: Ph- B-ALL: Low/Moderate-Intensity Regimens (Age >=65 / Unfit)
nodes.description: Attenuated regimens to reduce induction mortality while securing remission.
bullets: Inotuzumab ozogamicin + Dexamethasone (ALL-INITIAL-1): CD22 antibody-drug conjugate with short pulse dexamethasone; high CR rate with low toxicity.
Mini-hyper-CVD +/- Inotuzumab/Blinatumomab: Dose-reduced cyclophosphamide, vincristine, dexamethasone without anthracycline, alternating with low-dose methotrexate/cytarabine.
Low-intensity cytotoxic: Vincristine + Prednisone or POMP (mercaptopurine, vincristine, methotrexate, prednisone).
Comprehensive supportive care: TLS prophylaxis, prophylactic G-CSF, antifungal and antibacterial prophylaxis.

options.label: Induction completed - Proceed to response and MRD assessment

nodes.name: Ph- Post-Induction Response
nodes.title: Ph- B-ALL: Morphologic & MRD Response Assessment
nodes.description: Day 28-35 bone marrow evaluation for morphologic remission and measurable residual disease (MRD).
bullets: Morphologic CR: <5% bone marrow blasts, no circulating blasts, absence of extramedullary leukemia, ANC >=1000/mcL, platelets >=100,000/mcL.
MRD quantification: Highly sensitive 6-8 color multiparametric flow cytometry or NGS-based clonality assay (clonoSEQ, threshold <0.01% / 10^-4 blasts).

ECOG 1910 evidence: Demonstrates dramatic survival advantage when blinatumomab consolidation is added to chemotherapy in MRD-negative patients, and blinatumomab remains the standard of care for converting MRD-positive patients.

options.label: Complete Remission (CR) with MRD Negative (<0.01% blasts)
Complete Remission (CR) with Persistent MRD Positive (>=0.01% blasts)
Primary Refractory Disease / Incomplete Remission (<CR)

nodes.name: Ph- MRD- Consolidation
nodes.title: Ph- B-ALL: MRD-Negative Consolidation & Maintenance
nodes.description: Post-remission consolidation therapy with blinatumomab and maintenance.
bullets: ECOG 1910 Consolidation (Preferred): Multiagent consolidation chemotherapy alternating with Blinatumomab (4 cycles total: 2 cycles post-consolidation 1, 2 cycles post-consolidation 2). Proven overall survival benefit in MRD-negative adults <65y.

Allogeneic HCT Consideration: Strongly favored in first CR (CR1) for patients with poor-risk genetics: hypodiploidy (<44 chromosomes), KMT2A rearrangement (t(4;11)), TP53 mutation, Ph-like signature, or complex karyotype (>=5 abnormalities).
Standard Maintenance: POMP regimen (daily oral 6-mercaptopurine 50-75 mg/m2, weekly oral methotrexate 20 mg/m2, monthly pulses of IV vincristine and oral prednisone) for 2 to 3 years total duration.
CNS Surveillance & Prophylaxis: Complete full course of planned intrathecal chemotherapy injections during consolidation and early maintenance.

nodes.name: Ph- MRD+ Intensification
nodes.title: Ph- B-ALL: Persistent MRD Intensification & Allogeneic HCT
nodes.description: Targeted immunotherapy to eliminate persistent minimal residual disease prior to allogeneic transplant.
bullets: Blinatumomab (Preferred Standard of Care): Continuous IV infusion x 28 days (cycle 1: 9 mcg/d x 7 days then 28 mcg/d; subsequent cycles: 28 mcg/d). Achieves MRD conversion in ~80% of patients (BLAST study).
Monitor & Manage Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) and ICANS: Premedicate with dexamethasone; hold infusion and administer tocilizumab +/- dexamethasone if grade >=2 CRS occurs.
Allogeneic HCT (Strongly Recommended): Consolidate with myeloablative or reduced-intensity allogeneic HCT upon achieving MRD-negative status.
Alternative if blinatumomab contraindicated or unavailable: Multiagent chemotherapy intensification (e.g., high-dose cytarabine + fludarabine) or Inotuzumab ozogamicin.

nodes.name: T-ALL Age & Fitness
nodes.title: T-Cell ALL: Age & Clinical Cohort Stratification
nodes.description: Patient age and physiological fitness dictate frontline multiagent chemotherapy protocol selection.
bullets: AYA (15–39 years) without substantial comorbidities: pediatric-inspired regimens with augmented asparaginase and nelarabine for intermediate/high risk.
Adults 40–64 years: intensive adult protocols (Hyper-CVAD +/- nelarabine or dose-adjusted GRAALL-2014).
Adults >=65 years or with substantial comorbidities: dose-attenuated multiagent regimens or clinical trials.

options.label: AYA (Age 15–39 years) without substantial comorbidities
Adults (Age 40–64 years) without substantial comorbidities
Adults >=65 years or adults with substantial comorbidities

nodes.name: T-ALL Induction Regimens
nodes.title: T-ALL: Frontline Multiagent Induction Therapy
nodes.description: Multiagent chemotherapy induction protocols for T-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
bullets: AYA Preferred: COG AALL0434 backbone (daunorubicin, vincristine, prednisone, pegaspargase) with incorporation of Nelarabine (650 mg/m2 IV daily x 5) for patients with intermediate/high risk disease (dramatically lowers CNS relapse).
CALGB 10403 (Pediatric-inspired): Intensive 5-drug induction with pegaspargase, daunorubicin, vincristine, prednisone, and cyclophosphamide.
Adult Preferred: Hyper-CVAD (fractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, dexamethasone alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine) +/- Nelarabine.
GRAALL-2014: Multiagent regimen with dose adjustments based on age and tolerance.
CNS Prophylaxis: Robust intrathecal therapy (triple IT: methotrexate, cytarabine, hydrocortisone) mandatory due to higher baseline CNS predilection in T-ALL.

options.label: Induction completed - Proceed to response and MRD assessment

nodes.name: T-ALL Post-Induction Response
nodes.title: T-ALL: Morphologic & MRD Response Assessment
nodes.description: Day 28-35 bone marrow evaluation for morphologic remission and flow cytometric/NGS MRD.
bullets: Complete Remission (CR): <5% marrow blasts, no circulating blasts, resolution of mediastinal/extramedullary masses, peripheral count recovery.
MRD quantification: Flow cytometry (T-cell aberrant immunophenotype) or NGS TCR clonal rearrangement (sensitivity 10^-6).
High-risk classifiers: Early T-cell precursor (ETP-ALL), PTEN mutations, and NOTCH1/FBXW7 wild-type status carry increased relapse risk.

options.label: Complete Remission (CR) with MRD Negative
Complete Remission (CR) with Persistent MRD Positive
Primary Refractory Disease / Incomplete Remission (<CR)

nodes.name: T-ALL MRD- Consolidation
nodes.title: T-ALL: MRD-Negative Consolidation & Maintenance
nodes.description: Consolidation chemotherapy and transplant decision for standard and high-risk T-ALL.
bullets: Standard-Risk Chemotherapy Consolidation: Continue multiagent consolidation (e.g. COG AALL0434 or Hyper-CVAD blocks) followed by POMP maintenance for 2 to 3 years.

Allogeneic HCT in CR1: Strongly favored for patients with Early T-cell Precursor (ETP-ALL), poor cytogenetics (e.g. complex, MLL-r), or unfavorable molecular profile (NOTCH1/FBXW7 wild-type or PTEN mutations).
Nelarabine incorporation: If not administered during induction, consider adding nelarabine blocks during consolidation for young adults with CNS risk.
Surveillance: Serial marrow/MRD monitoring at months 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24.

nodes.name: T-ALL MRD+ Intensification
nodes.title: T-ALL: Persistent MRD Intensification & Allogeneic HCT
nodes.description: Intensification therapy to achieve deep remission before allogeneic transplantation.
bullets: Nelarabine-based Intensification: Administer Nelarabine (650 mg/m2 IV daily x 5 or 1500 mg/m2 days 1, 3, 5) alone or in combination with cyclophosphamide and etoposide.
Allogeneic HCT (Mandatory): Consolidate with allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant immediately once MRD negative status or minimum residual burden is reached.
Alternative regimens: High-dose cytarabine + fludarabine (FLAG-IDA) or venetoclax + decitabine/azacitidine under clinical trial or compassionate use.
Clinical Trial: Strongly consider enrolling on investigational cellular or targeted therapy protocols.

nodes.name: Relapsed/Refractory ALL
nodes.title: Relapsed or Primary Refractory ALL: Lineage & Subtype Classification
nodes.description: Identify disease lineage and actionable molecular targets in relapsed or refractory disease.
bullets: Repeat bone marrow aspirate and biopsy with comprehensive flow cytometry and cytogenetics/NGS.
Re-assess CD19, CD22, and CD38 expression prior to selecting targeted antibody or cellular immunotherapy.
For Ph+ B-ALL: immediate ABL1 kinase domain mutation analysis to guide TKI selection (specifically checking for T315I mutation).
Screen for extramedullary relapse: lumbar puncture for CSF involvement; imaging for testicular or nodal recurrence.

options.label: Relapsed / Refractory Ph+ B-ALL
Relapsed / Refractory Ph- B-ALL
Relapsed / Refractory T-ALL

nodes.name: R/R Ph+ B-ALL Salvage
nodes.title: Relapsed/Refractory Ph+ B-ALL: Targeted Immunotherapy & TKIs
nodes.description: Evidence-based salvage strategies integrating next-generation TKIs, immunotherapy, and cellular therapy.
bullets: Mutation-Directed TKI Selection: If T315I mutation present, use Ponatinib (45 mg daily) or Asciminib (with or without another TKI). For other resistance mutations, tailor to dasatinib, bosutinib, or nilotinib sensitivity profile.
Blinatumomab + TKI (Preferred): Ponatinib or dasatinib combined with blinatumomab demonstrates high complete remission and molecular clearance rates in relapsed/refractory Ph+ ALL.
Inotuzumab ozogamicin (CD22 ADC): Highly effective in CD22+ relapsed disease; monitor hepatic function and limit to 2-3 cycles if preceding allogeneic HCT.
CAR T-Cell Therapy (Brexucabtagene autoleucel): FDA-approved for adult relapsed/refractory B-ALL; tisagenlecleucel for patients aged <=25 years.
Allogeneic HCT / DLI: Second allogeneic HCT or donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) for eligible patients achieving subsequent remission.

nodes.name: R/R Ph- B-ALL Salvage
nodes.title: Relapsed/Refractory Ph- B-ALL: Immunotherapy & CAR-T Regimens
nodes.description: Targeted biologic and cellular therapies prioritized over conventional cytotoxic salvage.
bullets: Targeted Immunotherapy (Preferred over cytotoxic chemotherapy):
• Blinatumomab (CD19 BiTE): Continuous IV infusion x 28-day cycles; superior OS and response compared to standard salvage chemo (TOWER trial).

• Inotuzumab ozogamicin (CD22 ADC): 0.8 mg/m2 day 1, 0.5 mg/m2 days 8 & 15; superior CR rate over chemo (INO-VATE trial). Administer ursodiol and avoid dual-alkylator conditioning if bridging to HCT to prevent sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS/VOD).
Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-Cell Therapy:
• Brexucabtagene autoleucel (Tecartus): Indicated for adult relapsed/refractory B-ALL.
• Tisagenlecleucel (Kymriah): Indicated for pediatric and young adult patients <=25 years.
• Obecabtagene autoleucel (Apceth): Low-affinity CD19 CAR T-cell with reduced CRS profile.
Cytotoxic Salvage Regimens (if immunotherapy unavailable or as bridge): FLAG-IDA (fludarabine, cytarabine, idarubicin, G-CSF), mini-hyper-CVD + inotuzumab, or CLAG-M.
Allogeneic HCT: Essential consolidative therapy following attainment of second remission (CR2).

nodes.name: R/R T-ALL Salvage
nodes.title: Relapsed/Refractory T-ALL: Nelarabine & Targeted Regimens
nodes.description: Salvage therapy for relapsed or refractory T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
bullets: Nelarabine-based Therapy (Preferred): Nelarabine single agent (1500 mg/m2 days 1, 3, 5 every 21 days) or combination Nelarabine + Etoposide + Cyclophosphamide.
Targeted / Novel Approaches:
• Daratumumab (anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody): Promising activity in CD38-expressing relapsed/refractory T-ALL and ETP-ALL.
• Venetoclax + Decitabine or Azacitidine: BCL-2 inhibition active in early T-cell precursor (ETP) and immature T-ALL phenotypes.
• Menin inhibitors (e.g. revumenib): For KMT2A-rearranged cases.
Intensive Cytotoxic Chemotherapy: Augmented hyper-CVAD, FLAG-IDA, or clofarabine-based combinations.
Allogeneic HCT: Immediate HLA-matched donor mobilization to proceed to transplant upon attaining remission.
